blocks.text: Permanent Makeup Safety
Clean, Private, and Careful Permanent Makeup Appointments

Your safety matters before, during, and after your appointment. At Pomi B. Brow Studio, I work in a private, controlled studio setting with careful sanitation, single-use tools, disposable barriers, and clear preparation guidance.
This page explains how I prepare the space, handle tools, reduce cross-contamination risk, and help clients know when to ask questions before booking.
Ask Before Booking
[inline SVG illustration]
**Safety starts with the setup.**
Private appointments, clean surfaces, fresh barriers, and single-use tools.
Private studio
Appointments are focused on one client at a time.
Clean setup
Surfaces are cleaned and prepared before each session.
Single-use tools
Needles, tools, supplies, and pigment containers are used for one client.
Clear guidance
Preparation and aftercare help protect your healed result.
Start here
What makes permanent makeup safer?

Permanent makeup involves the skin, so safety starts with the full appointment process. A safer appointment includes a clean studio, fresh disposable barriers, single-use tools, careful pigment handling, gloves, masks, and clear aftercare instructions.
I want clients to feel comfortable asking questions. You should know how the space is prepared, what tools are used, and what to do before and after your appointment.
My approach
I do not want permanent makeup to feel rushed or unclear. Before we begin, the space is prepared, the service is reviewed, and the tools used for your appointment are handled with care.
Private environment
A controlled, one-client appointment setting
Permanent makeup requires focus, detail, and trust. A private appointment setting helps keep the visit calm and controlled.
Why privacy matters
I work with one client at a time so the appointment does not feel crowded or distracting. This helps keep attention on your service, your comfort, and your safety.
No crowded appointment space.
No unnecessary traffic around the work area.
More focus during detailed cosmetic work.
A calmer experience for personal services.
Why control matters
A controlled setup helps keep the work area clean and organized. Permanent makeup is detailed work, so the appointment space should support focus and cleanliness from start to finish.
Fresh setup for each appointment.
Clean work area before the service begins.
Organized tools and supplies.
Clear steps during the session.
Sanitation
Clean studio practices before each client
Clean surfaces, fresh barriers, and careful setup all help reduce unnecessary contact with the treatment area and tools.
Clean surfaces
Surfaces are disinfected and prepared between clients so the appointment starts with a clean work area.
Fresh barriers
Disposable barriers help protect surfaces and are replaced for each session.
Protective setup
Gloves, masks, and protective coverings are used as part of a clean appointment process.
What this means for you
You should not have to wonder whether the space is ready for your appointment. Clean setup and fresh barriers are part of the service process.
Single-use tools
Why single-use permanent makeup tools matter
Single-use tools help reduce cross-contamination risk because they are used for one client and then safely discarded.
Needles and cartridges
Needles and cartridges should be new for the appointment. I open these items in front of you so you know they are fresh and have not been used on anyone else.
Pigment containers
Pigment containers are used for one client only. This helps keep the pigment handling clean and prevents shared-use contamination.
Disposable supplies
Disposable tools and supplies are used during the appointment and discarded after the session. This keeps the process clean from client to client.
No reuse of single-use items
Items designed for single use should never be cleaned and reused. They should be disposed of after the appointment.
Client preparation
Your preparation also affects safety
A safe appointment is not only about the studio. Your skin, timing, health history, and aftercare also matter.
Arrive with healthy skin
Do not book over sunburn, cuts, irritation, breakouts, cold sores, or open skin.
Share health details
Tell the studio about medications, allergies, healing concerns, or medical conditions.
Plan your timing
Avoid booking too close to weddings, vacations, photo shoots, or major events.
Follow aftercare
Aftercare helps protect the treated area and supports the best healed result.
Before your appointment
Ask before booking if you recently had filler, Botox, laser, chemical peels, waxing, brow treatments, lip treatments, eye procedures, scalp treatments, or other cosmetic work near the treatment area.
Who should ask first
Who should ask before booking permanent makeup?
Some clients may still be good candidates, but timing matters. Please ask before booking if any of these apply to you.
Health and healing concerns
You are pregnant or nursing.
You take blood thinners.
You are prone to keloids.
You have a medical condition that affects healing.
You have allergies or past reactions to cosmetic products.
Treatment area concerns
You have irritation, cuts, sunburn, or open skin near the area.
You have active breakouts near the treatment area.
You have a cold sore history and want lip tint.
You have eye irritation and want eyeliner or lash enhancement.
You have scalp irritation and want scalp micropigmentation.
Medical questions

I can answer questions about the appointment process, but I cannot give medical clearance. For medical questions, medications, infections, skin conditions, or healing concerns, speak with your healthcare provider before scheduling.
By service
Safety considerations by service
Each service has different timing and preparation needs. Ask first if you are unsure.
Brows

Ask before booking microblading, powder brows, or shading if you have irritation, breakouts, sunburn, recent brow treatments, recent Botox, filler, laser, chemical peels, or sensitive skin near the brows.
Eyeliner and lash enhancement
Ask before booking if you have eye irritation, recent eye surgery, certain eye medications, recent cosmetic eye treatments, lash extensions, or sensitivity around the eyes.
Lip tint
Ask before booking if you have a cold sore history, active cold sore, cracked lips, irritation, recent filler, or recent treatments around the mouth.
Scalp micropigmentation
Ask before booking if you have scalp irritation, open skin, sunburn, active flaking, recent scalp treatments, or recent hair transplant work.
Aftercare
Safety continues after the appointment
Aftercare protects the treated area while it heals. Fresh pigment can look darker or brighter at first, then soften as the skin heals.
Protect the healing area
Do not pick, scratch, rub, or peel the treated area.
Avoid makeup directly on the healing area until cleared.
Avoid soaking, sauna, steam, swimming, and heavy sweating while healing.
Avoid sun exposure and harsh skincare near the area.
Know when to ask
Ask if you are unsure about aftercare products.
Ask if healing looks different than expected.
Ask before using active skincare near healed pigment.
Contact a physician for signs of infection or medical concerns.
Helpful aftercare page
Review the [Aftercare page](https://pomibrow.com/aftercare#top) before and after your appointment so you know what to avoid while healing.
FAQ
Permanent Makeup Safety FAQ
Is permanent makeup safe?
Permanent makeup is safest when done in a clean, controlled studio with proper sanitation, single-use tools, careful setup, and clear aftercare instructions.
What should I look for in a permanent makeup studio?

Look for a private, clean appointment setting, disinfected surfaces, fresh disposable barriers, single-use tools, pigment containers used for one client, gloves, masks, and clear aftercare instructions.
Are needles and tools reused?
No. Needles, cartridges, disposable tools, and single-use supplies are used for one client and then safely discarded.
Why are single-use tools important?
Single-use tools help reduce cross-contamination risk because they are not shared between clients or reused after the appointment.
Do you open needles in front of the client?
Yes. Needles and cartridges are opened in front of the client so you know they are new for your appointment.
Who should ask before booking?

Ask before booking if you are pregnant, nursing, taking blood thinners, prone to keloids, have active irritation, have a cold sore history for lip tint, have eye irritation for eye services, or recently had cosmetic treatments near the area.
Can I book if I have irritated skin?
Do not book over active irritation, cuts, sunburn, breakouts, cold sores, open skin, or scalp irritation. Ask first so timing can be handled safely.
Where is Pomi B. Brow Studio located?
Pomi B. Brow Studio is located at 2801 El Camino Real, Ste 13 in Tustin, CA, near Irvine and central Orange County.
Before you book
Review FAQ and aftercare information

Before scheduling, review the [FAQ page](https://pomibrow.com/faqs#top) and [Aftercare page](https://pomibrow.com/aftercare#top). These pages explain important preparation, healing, safety, and touch-up details.
Have a safety question before booking?
Contact Pomi B. Brow Studio in Tustin before scheduling. I can help you understand preparation, timing, aftercare, and whether you should ask additional questions before booking.
